title: Fuel prices increased, petrol by over Rs. 24
byline: The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (Ceypetco) has announced a significant revision of fuel prices effective from midnight today (09) in the wake of rising global fuel prices owing to the Middle East conflict.

title: Another gunman arrested over Jinthupitiya shooting incident
byline: Another gunman involved in the shooting that killed a man and injured two children in Jinthupitiya recently has been arrested.

title: Oil prices fall after Trump signals that war will end soon
byline: Global oil prices fell in early Tuesday morning trading in Asia.

title: US has not ‘won enough’ yet, Trump says as he claims war will be over ‘pretty quickly’
byline: Donald Trump has said the US has not “won enough” in Iran, as he claimed that the conflict will be over “pretty quickly” during a press conference.

title: Mainly dry weather expected in most parts of the island
byline: A few showers are likely in Northern Province and in Trincomalee and Anuradhapura districts, today (10), the Department of Meteorology said.

title: UAE condemns Iran’s attempted ballistic missile strike on Turkey
byline: The United Arab Emirates strongly condemned on Monday Iran’s attempt to target Turkey with a ballistic missile, marking the second such incident in less than a week.

title: France to deploy nearly a dozen warships, mulls Hormuz mission, Macron says
byline: France is sending about a dozen naval vessels, including its aircraft carrier strike group, to the Mediterranean, Red Sea, and potentially the Strait of Hormuz, as part of defensive support for allies threatened by the Middle East conflict.

title: Five Iranian women’s soccer players granted humanitarian visas in Australia
byline: Australia on Tuesday granted humanitarian visas to five Iranian women’s soccer team players after they sought asylum fearing persecution in their home nation.

title: PM Harini highlights importance of recognising women’s unpaid care work
byline: Prime Minister Dr Harini Amarasuriya today participated in the International Women’s Day Flagship Event hosted by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) at the ADB Headquarters in Manila, Philippines.

title: Fuel prices increased to manage stocks and stabilize Market, officials say
byline: The Managing Director of the Ceylon Petroleum Storage Terminals Limited (CPSTL), Mayura Neththikumarage has explained today (10) the reasons for yesterday’s increase in fuel prices in the country.

title: School van charges raised by 5% with effect from today
byline: With the recent surge in fuel prices, the All Ceylon School Children’s Transport Association has decided to increase school transport fees by 5%, effective from today (10).

title: ‘More fun to sink them’: Trump on destruction of 46 Iranian naval ships
byline: US President Donald Trump on Monday claimed that the US Navy has sunk 46 “top-of-the-line” Iranian naval ships so far.

title: Functions of RTI Commission to be digitized
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has granted approval to the proposal to implement a project for the digitalization of the operational activities of the Right to Information Commission.

title: Bodies of sailors killed in warship sinking near Sri Lanka will be repatriated: Iran
byline: Iran says the bodies of dozens of sailors killed when the US attacked and sank IRIS Dena vessel near close to Sri Lanka will soon be returned to the country.

title: Arrangements in place for uninterrupted supply of fuel & energy for two months: President
byline: Arrangements are in place for an uninterrupted supply of fuel and energy for two more months despite the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake stated.

title: Peradeniya Uni students stage torchlight protest alleging curbs on student freedom
byline: A group of students of the University of Peradeniya held a torchlight protest today at the Galaha Junction, to voice opposition to what they describe as increasing restrictions on student freedoms.

title: More members of Iranian soccer team seek asylum as most of squad leaves Australia
byline: Seven members of the Iranian women’s soccer team have remained in Australia, while the rest of the squad has now left the country for Iran, according to CNN.

title: North Korea’s Kim Yo Jong says US-South Korea drills to harm regional stability
byline: North Korea’s Kim Yo Jong, the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said U.S.-South Korea military drills that began this week were a “provocative and aggressive war rehearsal” that would harm regional stability, state media KCNA reported on Tuesday.

title: ‘We will decide when to end war, not US’: Iran’s sharp response to Trump
byline: Tehran has responded to US President Donald Trump’s remark about ending the war in Iran, saying it will be the one who will “determine” when the military actions against American and Israeli targets cease.

title: SC postpones hearing of Mahindananda and Nalin’s appeal petitions to tomorrow
byline: The Supreme Court has adjourned until tomorrow (11) the hearing of the appeal petitions filed by former ministers Mahindananda Aluthgamage and Nalin Fernando against the prison sentences imposed on them over corruption charges.

title: Woman arrested with 100g of ‘Ice’ in Rathmalana
byline: A woman has been arrested in the Rathmalana area for the possession of 100 grams of Crystal Methamphetamine, commonly known as ‘Ice’, police said.

title: Over 600kg of narcotics discovered in multi-day trawler seized by navy: Minister
byline: Over 600 kilograms of narcotics have been discovered in the multi-day fishing vessel seized by the Sri Lanka Navy on suspicion of transporting a consignment of drugs, according to Minister of Public Security and Parliamentary Affairs Ananda Wijepala.

title: No revision of bus fares despite fuel price hike - NTC
byline: The National Transport Commission (NTC) has announced that bus fares will not be revised despite the recent increase in fuel prices.

title: Israel has been illegally using white phosphorus in Lebanon: Human Rights Watch
byline: The Israeli military illegally used white phosphorus munitions over homes in the southern Lebanese town Yohmor on March 3, posing a threat to civilians, Human Rights Watch said in a report on Monday.

title: Former DIG of CID arrested by Bribery Commission
byline: The former Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), Prasad Ranasinghe, has been arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) for allegedly obstructing investigations.

title: UK parliament votes to reject social media ban for under-16s
byline: A ban on social media for under-16s has been rejected by members of parliament in the UK.

title: Peace loving country like India should be UNSC permanent member: Opposition Leader
byline: Leader of the Opposition of Sri Lanka Sajith Premadasa on Monday said that a peace-loving country like India should be made a permanent member in the United Nations.

title: Australia to send missiles to UAE, deploy military surveillance aircraft
byline: Australia will deploy a military surveillance aircraft to the Middle East and send missiles to the United Arab Emirates but will not put troops on the ground in Iran, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Tuesday.

title: Former DIG of CID Prasad Ranasinghe granted bail
byline: Former Deputy Inspector General of Police of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) Prasad Ranasinghe who was arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) for allegedly obstructing investigations has been granted bail.

title: SC resumes hearing of appeals by ex-ministers Mahindananda and Nalin Fernando for second day
byline: The hearing of the appeal filed by former ministers Mahindananda Aluthgamage and Nalin Fernando, challenging the prison sentences imposed on them over corruption charges, has been commenced for the second day today (10) before the Supreme Court.

title: Tuesday will be most intense day of strikes on Iran, Hegseth says
byline: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Tuesday would be the most intense ⁠day of strikes against Iran in the campaign so far.

title: WHO warns of health risks from ‘black rain’ in Iran
byline: The World Health Organization warned on Tuesday that the “black rain” falling in Iran after strikes on oil facilities could cause respiratory problems, and it backed Iran’s advisory urging people to remain indoors.

title: Agreement signed to hand over vehicle number plate printing to new company
byline: The printing of number plates for motor vehicles has been handed over to a new company, with the relevant agreement signed today (10).

title: 191 injured in Israel over last 24 hours as conflict with Iran intensifies: Israeli Health Ministry
byline: Figures released by the Israeli Ministry of Health and published by the Times of Israel reveal that a total of 191 individuals sustained injuries over the last 24 hours amid the continuing hostilities with Iran.

title: Iran says oil blockade will continue until attacks end, Trump threatens to escalate strikes
byline: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Tuesday they would not allow “one litre of oil” to be shipped from the Middle East if US and Israeli attacks continue, prompting a warning from President Donald Trump that the US would hit Iran much harder if it blocked exports from the vital energy-producing region.

title: Public urged to reduce non-essential travel and conserve fuel amid global energy crisis
byline: The Chairman of the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC), D.J. Rajakaruna, has requested the public to reduce non-essential travel and use fuel sparingly in order to manage the energy crisis arising from the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East.

title: PM Harini holds bilateral talks in Philippines to enhance cooperation in education and other sectors
byline: Prime Minister of Sri Lanka Dr. Harini Amarasuriya held a series of meetings with key Philippine institutions during her ongoing official visit to the Philippines from 09–11 March 2026, focusing on strengthening cooperation in education, higher education, technical skills development, and agricultural research.

title: Oil sinks 7% as Trump predicts Middle East de-escalation
byline: Oil prices plummeted 7% on Tuesday after soaring to a more than three-year high in the previous session as U.S. President Donald Trump predicted the war in the Middle East could end soon, easing concerns about prolonged disruptions to oil supplies.

title: Putin, in a phone call with Trump, shares proposals to end Iran war quickly
byline: Russian President Vladimir Putin, in a telephone conversation on Monday with U.S. President Donald Trump, put forward proposals for a quick settlement of the conflict around Iran, Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said.

title: Netanyahu says Israel will continue Iran strikes
byline: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed Tuesday that Israel will continue striking Iran.

title: Litro Gas prices increased
byline: The prices of Litro domestic LP gas cylinders have been increased with effect from midnight today (10), the Litro Gas Company has announced.

title: Electricity TUs to continue their strike as talks with authorities end in deadlock
byline: A number of electricity trade unions have announced that they will continue their strike action over several demands.

title: 16-hour water cut in Negombo and Katana on Thursday
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) has announced a 16-hour water supply suspension affecting the Negombo and Katana areas on March 12.

title: Govt. should use funds in treasury to provide concessions instead of increasing fuel prices – Harsha
byline: The government should utilize the funds in the treasury to provide concessions to the general public instead of increasing fuel prices in line with global developments, the Chairman of the Committee on Public Finance (CoPF), Member of Parliament Harsha de Silva stated.

title: Iranian foreign minister says negotiations with U.S. may be off the table
byline: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Monday that talks with the United States may be off the table after the U.S. and Israel initiated a military operation against the country.

title: Oil could hit $150 a barrel despite Trump’s reassurances, expert warns
byline: The US-Israel war with Iran has triggered the biggest oil disruption in history, as the critical Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed, with some experts estimating oil could hit $150 per barrel by the end of March.

title: Navy seizes fishing trawler suspected of carrying narcotics haul and weapons
byline: A multi-day fishing trawler transporting a stock of sacks suspected to contain narcotics and weapons was seized during a special operation conducted in the deep seas off the southern coast of Sri Lanka.

title: Fifth National Oral Health Survey in Sri Lanka begins today – Health Ministry
byline: The Ministry of Health states that the Fifth National Oral Health Survey in Sri Lanka will commence today (10).

title: CEB subsidiaries agree to 62 of 64 union demands
byline: The boards of four key subsidiary companies linked to the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) have agreed to 62 out of 64 demands presented by trade unions following discussions held with union representatives.

title: President pledges to introduce national policy to upgrade Sri Lanka’s public transport system
byline: It is the government’s expectation to establish a strong public transport system that is comfortable, safe, efficient and reliable for the people and that the government is currently in the process of formulating a national policy to achieve this objective, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake stated.

title: Trump warns of ‘death, fire, and fury’ if Iran disrupts global oil passageway
byline: President Trump has issued another warning to Iran about disrupting shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Strike delays restoration of power disruptions in several areas
byline: The restoration of the prevailing electricity disruptions in Colombo 9, Colombo 14, and several areas in Gampaha is expected to take some time due to an ongoing strike launched by trade unions.
